title: Jimmy Blanton's death and carrying Babs Gonzales to the doctor
summary: Jones recalls Blanton's death around 1941 and carrying a collapsed Babs Gonzales to Doc Hawkins for hospital admission.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Jimmy Blanton died. I was to the hospital because Black Dot had the place there where there used to a guy named Gap-Eye used to have a Cadillac. He'd go out all the time when I was hanging out with Doc Hawkins.
Do you know what year that was, Jo?
1940-41, it was hectic in there. It was around about '41, because I remember I was across the street because we had played out to another club and

Babs Gonzales was shooting pool and he fell and wouldn't let nobody pick him up. I came up and took him to Doctor Hawkins in my arms. I took him in my hand, in my own arms and took him across the street and Doc Hawkins had him admitted to a hospital because Babs was collapsed. He was going to go right into TB; he was going to die, because he was running around, you know, he was just hanging around with musicians.
Very glad to have him there in the rhythm section.
